notes: Length uniformity alone is strictly weaker than random descent - 126 bordered length-preserving rules with |l| = 4, 5 are length-uniform on words <= 10 but not confluent (e.g. aaaba -> baabb on aaabaaaba).
novelty_basis: Two web searches (2026-10-18) found no statement; closest work studies the structure of derivations of length-preserving one-rule systems (Inform. Comput., 2015, doi 10.1016/j.ic.2015.07.002). Elementary enough to be folklore; pending Historian audit.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C04.md Theorem 2); abstract consequence and the length-changing case Lean-verified (steps_length_unique, length_changing_unique); potential checked on 5365 rules / 470,927 steps; awaiting independent skeptic review
statement:
For every rule l -> r (l != r) over a finite alphabet there are Phi : words -> Z and delta != 0 with
Phi(v) = Phi(u) + delta for every step u -> v (Phi = length if |l| != |r|; otherwise
Phi(w) = sum of i^K over positions i carrying a suitable letter c, K the least exponent at which the power
sums of the c-positions of l and r differ). Consequently all derivations between two given words have the same
number of steps, and a terminating one-rule system is confluent iff it has random descent.
title: Every one-rule system has a constant-step potential; for terminating ones confluence is equivalent to random descent
